clause: Batch runner core on kernel Job Runtime (headless/quiet) [STU-AUT-012]

scope.summary: Implement the native batch runner that applies a command sequence or macro over a set of input files and writes results without code. It executes on the kernel Job Runtime as a headless, bounded, quiet job: no foreground window, no focus steal, no input hijack; progress and per-file results surface through structured job state, not modal UI. Every processed file emits a receipt and each mutating output passes sandbox -> validation -> PromotionGate.
acceptance_criteria: batch runner on Job Runtime; headless/quiet; per-file receipts + promotion; observable job state
proof_targets: headless batch run + focus-audit negative + receipts
expected_tests: live: batch runs a macro over a file set headless; per-file receipts emitted
negative: batch run does not steal focus / pop foreground window
argus: batch panel progress observable by author_id

risk_if_missed: No batch automation, or batch violates the headless/quiet law.

risks: Scaffold-only claim without runtime proof (Spec-Realism Gate).
Domain MT forking a canonical primitive instead of referencing 14.23.
SQLite creep on a studio_* write path.
minimum_controls: At least one proof command exercises executable runtime or a Handshake-managed resource boundary.
Reference canonical primitives (14.23); no shadow primitives.
